assumptions: The private service book is clearly distinguished from a statutory EU product or battery passport and stores owner data only with explicit consent.

Safety-sensitive compatibility and diagnostic decisions remain technician-approved, and manufacturer datasets are linked, licensed, or built from lawful individual observations rather than copied wholesale.
The family installation company provides a real internal pilot but is not treated as evidence that unrelated installers will adopt or pay.
The two-sided marketplace is deferred until the registry demonstrates repeat service demand, and specialist insurance, privacy, and electrical-safety advice is purchased when needed.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: A portable, owner-authorised lifecycle record can bridge fragmented installer and manufacturer portals and improve handover, warranty, transfer, and service continuity. The insight is weakened by existing QR handover products and by the fact that current statutory DPP rules do not cover all renewable equipment.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: A 1.6 million-plus Polish micro-installation base provides many potential service events, and avoided callbacks or retained maintenance can support payment. Actual service frequency and willingness to pay are unknown, owners may value portability more than installers do, and some installers may resist a record that reduces their service lock-in.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: A registry can have 80-90% software gross margin and recurring subscriptions, while service events create later transaction revenue. Basic passport pricing is already very low, and the founder-wealth path depends on 1200 installers plus 25000 annual transactions and authorised data revenue; CAC, support, service conversion, take rate, insurance, and marketplace margins are unvalidated.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Polish residential batteries and inverters form a sufficiently narrow first segment inside a very large installed PV base, and the family company can expose real assets and service calls. Falling residential new-install share makes an installed-base wedge important but does not erase the meaningful aftermarket.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Cross-manufacturer portability and an owner-controlled record may differentiate the product locally. SolarPlus, InsTool, Payaca, and manufacturer portals already cover handover, QR documents, customer records, and broader installer workflows, while a public EU repair platform reduces the prospect of controlling a generic directory.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A successful identity and lifecycle layer can extend from batteries and inverters to heat pumps, more installers, other countries, warranty workflows, authorised parts, service routing, and data APIs. Each step requires reliable data rights, technician governance, and operational capacity, especially once transactions begin.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Persistent asset identities and lawfully accumulated configuration, failure, service, and verified-transaction histories can compound over years. Portability limits artificial lock-in, manufacturers can restrict access, incumbents can bundle records, and the valuable compatibility layer depends on licences or painstaking lawful data creation.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: One owner-controlled cross-vendor QR record could be materially more convenient than scattered portals during transfer or repair. The packet does not yet show fewer callbacks, faster diagnosis, more retained service, or better parts matching, and a simple passport is a low-price commodity rather than a strong standalone advantage.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The 2027 battery-passport requirement, right-to-repair direction, and a large aging installed base make lifecycle records and aftermarket service timely. Product-specific delegated acts and a contracting new-install share mean regulation should be treated as adjacency and service demand, not automatic adoption.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: The family company supplies unusually cheap access to an authentic pilot, and wholesalers or service networks could later aggregate installers. That advantage proves neither external adoption nor a scalable channel; installer referrals, partner bundles, consent, and paid conversion still need direct evidence.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: A narrow record and document-linking MVP fits 70000 PLN, 12-18 weekly hours, the founder's technical skills, and a low-camera workflow. Privacy and physical-security exposure, unsafe matching, manufacturer data rights, insurance, dispute handling, and marketplace support make the later model substantially harder and require delegated experts.

main_structural_strength: The founder has direct, low-cost access to real renewable-equipment handovers and service calls, allowing a persistent asset record to be tested against recurring lifecycle events before broader marketplace investment.
primary_score_limiter: The owner benefits most from portability while the proposed payer may prefer lock-in, and defensible economics depend on unproven aftermarket transactions because basic handover and passport records are already bundled or cheaply priced.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: SolarPlus, InsTool, and Payaca already provide handover or QR customer records, manufacturer portals already bind equipment to installers, and Collecta's published passport pricing shows that simple record generation has little pricing power.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A 50-100 asset family-company pilot and a separate paid installer cohort should establish owner activation and consent, record-maintenance and transfer rates, avoided callbacks or faster resolutions, annual installer payback, repeat service conversion, lawful data access, and verified transaction contribution margin before any marketplace build.
highest_value_structural_change: Make the portable record free or near-cost and focus first on technician-verified battery and inverter service orchestration, monetising measurable installer workflow savings and completed service or parts events instead of charging primarily for passport creation.
